title: Administrator
description:

title: Business Development Executive
salary_text: £30000 - £35000 per year (Phone, Laptop, Car Allowance, Bonus)
description:
We are currently seeking an ambitious and commercially focused Business Development Executive to help drive business growth across our Construction & Highways operations.

This is a customer-facing role responsible for developing new business opportunities, strengthening existing client relationships and delivering profitable growth. Working closely with our Commercial, Operations and Transport teams, you will identify customer requirements, prepare quotations and proposals, and ensure a smooth transition from sale to delivery.

The role combines field-based customer engagement with office-based sales activity and would suit someone who enjoys building relationships, identifying opportunities and achieving measurable results.

Key Responsibilities

Develop and grow relationships with existing customers while identifying and securing new business opportunities.

Maintain regular contact with clients through meetings, site visits and telephone communication.

Qualify customer requirements and prepare accurate quotations, estimates and proposals.

Follow up quotations and proposals to maximise conversion opportunities.

Work closely with operational teams to coordinate resources and ensure successful project delivery.

Identify and target prospective customers within key market sectors.

Maintain accurate customer records and sales information within company systems.

Analyse customer activity and sales performance against targets.

Produce weekly and monthly sales reports.

Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and business development planning.

Promote and uphold the company's health, safety and quality standards.

What We're Looking For

Essential

Previous sales or business development experience.

Strong customer relationship management skills.

Excellent communication and presentation abilities.

Ability to identify opportunities and convert them into business.

Strong organisational and time management skills.

Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.

A proactive and self-motivated approach.

Desirable
- Experience within construction, highways, civil engineering industries.
- Familiarity with project planning or project management.
- Experience analysing sales or business data.
- Knowledge of road planing or surfacing operations.

If this sounds like you hit the apply button.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
About the Business

A great opportunity to join a large, well-established services business based in Worcester as a Finance Assistant, paying £27,000 - £31,000 per annum, with hybrid and flexible working. Reporting to an Assistant Management Accountant, you'll support month end and reporting for the wider finance team. The role suits someone who is AAT qualified, studying, or keen to start.

Main Duties:

As a Finance Assistant, your main duties include:
- Posting journals, recharges and everyday accounting adjustments accurately and within agreed deadlines
- Helping to prepare accruals, prepayments and supporting schedules during month end
- Keeping financial records, working files and backing documents complete and up to date in the finance and reporting systems
- Assisting with balance sheet and control account reconciliations, looking into routine differences and raising anything that needs escalating
- Helping to put together the monthly management accounts packs and other reports
- Pulling together records and evidence for both the internal and external auditors
- Following finance policies and controls, and flagging errors, exceptions or possible control issues
- Getting involved in process improvements and team projects that make finance more efficient
- Building your knowledge of accounting principles, controls, reporting and the finance systems
- Supporting wider projects across the business when needed

Location / Office / Culture

The role is hybrid, based in Worcester, with three days a week in the office and very flexible working. You'll be part of a larger finance team, working closely with the management accountants and learning the month-end process from start to finish.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience in a finance role is essential
- Experience processing and checking financial information accurately
- Experience using an ERP or finance system
- GCSE English and Maths at grade 4/C or above (or equivalent)
- AAT qualified, currently studying, or keen to start
- Comfortable working to deadlines and prioritising your own workload
- Able to look into problems and work out what has gone wrong
- Strong attention to detail, good communication skills and basic Microsoft 365

Why Join the business
- Hybrid working, three days in the office
- Very flexible working
- Study support
- Broad exposure to month end, reconciliations and audit
- A solid grounding for a future management accounting career
- Large, well-established business

About Us

We are a local accountancy recruitment specialist. We appreciate that roles are often online for a long period of time. If you want to check if this role is still live or just want more details before applying, call us directly.

title: Finance Assistant
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company
Finance Assistant
Location: Worcester Salary: £27,000
Working pattern: Hybrid, three days in the office and two days from home
Hours: 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 5:00pm
Job type: Permanent, full-time
Are you an experienced Finance Assistant looking for a broader role with exposure to month-end accounting?
An established and successful organisation based in the Worcester area is looking to recruit a Finance Assistant into its finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with transactional finance experience who would like to develop their knowledge of balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, prepayments and international accounting.
The position offers a varied workload covering purchase ledger, bank reconciliations, expenses, and month-end support. You will work closely with an experienced finance team and have the opportunity to develop your accounting knowledge while taking ownership of several important processes.
Your new role
- Processing purchase invoices and maintaining accurate ledger records
- Reviewing the purchase ledger and resolving supplier queries
- Preparing supplier payment runs and ensuring payments are made in line with agreed terms
- Completing daily bank reconciliations
- Supporting the month-end process
- Assisting with balance sheet reconciliations, accruals and prepayments
- Raising intercompany invoices and completing intercompany reconciliations
- Preparing information to support VAT returns
- Producing expenditure analysis and spend-versus-budget reports
- Supporting customer invoice queries and processing approved credit notes

What you'll need to succeed
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant, Finance Assistant, Assistant Accountant or similar position
- Practical experience across purchase ledger, cash book or nominal ledger accounting
- Experience completing bank reconciliations
- An understanding of accruals, prepayments and balance sheet reconciliations
- Good Excel skills, including the ability to create and manipulate spreadsheets
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to prioritise a varied workload
- A proactive, flexible and team-focused approach

An AAT qualification or current AAT studies would be advantageous but are not essential. Additional language skills would also be useful, although they are not required.
What you'll get in return
- Salary of £27,000
- Hybrid working, with three days in the office and two days from home
- A 35-hour working week
- Broad exposure across transactional finance and month-end accounting
- Support from an established finance team
- The opportunity to develop towards a more senior accounting position

This role would be particularly suitable for an experienced transactional finance professional who is ready to broaden their responsibilities and gain more meaningful month-end exposure.
What you need to do now

If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.
If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.

Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator

An initial 6 month role with possibility of going permanent

Up to 27k + increments upon completing training

5 days on site for 3 months

Location: Worcestershire

Hours: Full-Time, 37.5 Hours per Week (Monday to Friday)

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

We are recruiting on behalf of our client for a Payroll Administrator to join their Finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented and organised professional looking to develop their career within payroll, supporting both UK and international payroll operations.

Working closely with an experienced payroll team, you will help ensure payrolls are processed accurately, compliantly and on time, while providing a high standard of service to internal stakeholders, contractors and external providers.

The Role

The successful candidate will support the delivery of an effective payroll service across multiple payrolls and jurisdictions.

Key responsibilities include:
- Assisting with the accurate and timely processing of payrolls.
- Working alongside senior payroll colleagues to ensure payroll deadlines are met.
- Liaising with employees, contractors and external providers to resolve payroll-related queries.
- Supporting the administration of international payrolls through third-party payroll providers.
- Assisting with compliance requirements and payroll documentation for overseas jurisdictions.
- Ensuring timesheets, invoices and expense information are received and processed on schedule.
- Maintaining payroll records and systems with a high degree of accuracy.
- Monitoring payroll processes and identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Supporting business managers by communicating payroll issues and contractor-related concerns.
- Keeping informed of relevant legislative changes affecting payroll, tax and employment practices.
- Providing excellent customer service to both internal and external stakeholders.

About You

We are seeking a highly organised individual with strong administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Strong verbal and written communication skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads effectively.
- Strong customer service focus.
- Ability to investigate and resolve problems logically.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable Experience
- A minimum of 12 months' payroll experience or experience in a similar finance or administration role.
- Exposure to payroll systems and payroll processing.
- Experience working with international payrolls would be advantageous.

Qualifications

GCSEs (or equivalent) including English Language and Mathematics at Grade C/4 or above.

Additional Advantage

Spanish language skills would be highly advantageous, particularly when supporting international payroll activities and communicating with overseas stakeholders.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing and collaborative organisation where you will gain exposure to both UK and international payroll operations. The role offers variety, responsibility and the chance to develop specialist payroll knowledge while working alongside experienced professionals.

If you are an organised administrator with payroll experience and a passion for accuracy and customer service, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

title: Quality Administrator
description:
Exciting Opportunity: Administrative Support for Quality Function

Our client, a prominent organisation in the manufacturing sector, is seeking two motivated individuals to join their Quality function on a fixed-term contract. This is a fantastic opportunity to contribute to ensuring the timely release of products, while enhancing your skills in a dynamic environment!

Position: Quality Administrator

Location: Worcester,

Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract (6 months) rolling
Hourly Rate: 18.00 PAYE
Working Pattern: Full Time (37.5 hours per week, approx. 7.5 hours per day; flexibility available with potential overtime)

Key Responsibilities:
- Process concessions (Quality Notifications) within SAP to ensure compliance and quality standards.
- Assist Quality Technicians in maintaining equipment calibration, contributing to operational excellence.
- Support the product release process, playing a vital role in the quality assurance workflow.
- Archive Production Orders, ensuring accurate record-keeping and accessibility.

Skills & Qualifications:
- Prior experience in a similar administrative role is advantageous and will be beneficial.
- Proficiency in SAP, especially in processing Quality Notifications, or experience with other ERP systems and Quality tools is preferred.
- Experience in a manufacturing environment is desirable, but not essential.
- Comfortable and skilled in using IT systems, enabling efficient task completion.

Desired Behaviours:
- Ability to integrate into and support a small, high-performing team, contributing positively to team dynamics.
- A proactive willingness to learn new skills and adapt to evolving processes.

Why This Role?
This role offers the chance to work within a committed team dedicated to quality assurance. The employer values its employees and provides a supportive environment for professional development. The organisation is known for its high standards and commitment to quality, making this an ideal place for individuals who thrive in a structured yet flexible setting.

How to Apply:
If you are ready to take on this challenge and contribute to a quality-driven team, consider applying for this role today! This is a remarkable opportunity to enhance your administrative skills while supporting a critical function within the organisation.

Candidates who meet the qualifications are encouraged to apply promptly, as this role is expected to attract significant interest. Embrace the chance to make a difference in the Quality function with our client!

Note: Only candidates who meet the specified requirements will be contacted for an interview. Thank you for considering this opportunity with our client.

We use generative AI tools to support our candidate screening process. This helps us ensure a fair, consistent, and efficient experience for all applicants. Rest assured, all final decisions are made by our hiring team, and your application will be reviewed with care and attention.

Adecco is a disability-confident employer. It is important to us that we run an inclusive and accessible recruitment process to support candidates of all backgrounds and all abilities to apply. Adecco is committed to building a supportive environment for you to explore the next steps in your career. If you require reasonable adjustments at any stage, please let us know and we will be happy to support you.

title: Administrator
company: Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Herefordshire and Worcestershire Health and Care NHS Trust
description: Are you an enthusiastic and motivated individual with a positive attitude? Are you looking for a new and exciting challenge? We are looking to recruit a Band 3 Administrator 22.5 hours per week over 5 days over a 7 day period, in our busy Neighbourhood Team, where you will be based in a central location in Worcester City. This is a busy and varied role, which requires the post holder to have a flexible approach, a calm, professional manner who can work both independently and as part of a team. You will have a working knowledge of Microsoft office and an understanding of the Data Protection Act and NHS Code of Conduct. You will also have excellent communication and interpersonal skills, which will support you in dealing with telephone enquiries from patients, relatives and other professionals such as GPS and outside agencies. Applicants must read the attached guidance notes before submitting your application for full understanding of Trust requirements. You will be part of the busy admin team for the community nursing staff, Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy. You will undertake a vital role in supporting the team with admin duties including telephone duties, monitoring email inboxes, and supporting all our clinical staff. This role will include contact with patients, carers, professionals, and family members. You will also need to be highly organised have great self-motivation and be a team player. Be able to solve problems that arise and support other teams within the service at short notice. The ability to prioritise a busy workload and work flexibly and meet deadlines is a requirement of the role as we are very focused on providing the very best customer service for our service users. Administration duties specific to the role. Providing support as required e.g. telephone cover, email inbox management, scanning, diary management, maintaining accurate records, packing online prescription orders. Within this role you will have contact with emotional and distressed patients and family members, a calm telephone manner is essential, but training and support will be provided. For full details of the duties and criteria for the role please refer to the job description and person specification attached.
